question: What is the main goal of blood glucose monitoring during pregnancy for diabetic women?

options.A: Maintaining near-normal blood sugar levels without causing severe hypoglycemia
options.B: Completely eliminating the need for any carbohydrate intake in diet
options.C: Predicting the exact birth weight of the baby down to the gram
options.D: Ensuring the mother's pancreas starts producing insulin again

explanation: The main aim is tight control to protect the fetus while keeping the mother safe from dangerously low blood sugar. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T3#BMP221_U4_T3_h6)

question: What type of questions should make up the majority of an interview guide?

options.A: Yes-or-no questions
options.B: Strictly numerical questions
options.C: Multiple-choice questions
options.D: Open-ended questions

explanation: Open-ended questions encourage participants to share detailed stories and feelings in their own words. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T2#BMP225_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is a key reason for conducting regular wound checks?

options.A: To ensure the patient never feels any pain during healing
options.B: To catch early signs of complications and guide care decisions
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for wound dressings
options.D: To speed up natural skin color restoration after trauma

explanation: Regular assessment allows midwives to monitor healing progress and detect early complications like infection or wound breakdown. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier keeping adolescents away from health clinics?

options.A: Harsh and scolding attitudes from health workers
options.B: Free and unlimited access to youth clinics
options.C: Fear of community members judging them
options.D: Clinic hours that clash with school timetables

explanation: Free and open access encourages attendance rather than acting as a barrier; teenagers are actually deterred by costs, poor attitudes, and bad timing. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T9#BMP126_U2_T9_h3)

question: How does dropping out of school due to early pregnancy affect the long-term well-being of a young mother?

options.A: It guarantees she will receive financial support from the government
options.B: It gives her more time to focus entirely on learning traditional crafts
options.C: It improves her mental health by removing academic stress
options.D: It limits her future job prospects and keeps her trapped in poverty

explanation: Without a solid education or professional skills, finding stable, well-paying employment becomes extremely difficult, perpetuating financial hardship. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T2#BMP320_U3_T2_h5)

question: If a woman has a roomy gynecoid pelvis, what does this mean for the baby during labour?

options.A: The baby's head will remain unengaged until pushing begins
options.B: The baby will experience immediate shoulder dystocia at the inlet
options.C: The baby will find it easy to turn its head inside the pelvis
options.D: The baby is forced to stay in a breech position

explanation: A roomy mid-pelvis with good side-to-side space supports smooth internal rotation of the baby's head during the second stage of labour. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T3#BMP210_U1_T3_h3)

question: What simple action can a midwife take to help soothe mild pain during a procedure for a newborn?

options.A: Placing the infant in a brightly lit room
options.B: Encouraging loud vocalization to release tension
options.C: Administering a small amount of oral sucrose solution
options.D: Applying cold ice packs directly to the chest

explanation: Sweet-tasting sugar water combined with sucking on a clean finger or dummy helps activate natural pain-relief pathways in babies. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T1#BMP220_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the most effective way to share health education during a village outreach clinic?

options.A: Reading long scientific journal articles aloud to silent crowds
options.B: Using interactive group discussions in the local language
options.C: Leaving pamphlets on a table without speaking to anyone
options.D: Handing out complex medical textbooks written in English

explanation: Interactive talks in local languages engage the women, encourage questions, and ensure the health messages are properly understood. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T2#BMP215_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is it important for midwives to know about antidepressant therapy?

options.A: Midwives must replace the role of psychiatric specialists completely
options.B: Midwives diagnose all complex mental health disorders in labor
options.C: Midwives frequently care for pregnant women experiencing psychological distress
options.D: Midwives are legally required to prescribe psychiatric medications

explanation: Knowing about these treatments helps midwives support expectant mothers, watch for side effects, and connect them with the right care team. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common side effect of opioids during labour?

options.A: Nausea and active vomiting
options.B: Persistent high fever and chills
options.C: Delayed stomach emptying
options.D: Dizziness and heavy drowsiness

explanation: Opioids cause sedation, nausea, and slowed digestion, but they do not typically cause fever or chills. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h5)

question: What blood test is done on an exposed infant around 9 to 12 months of age to check for immunity?

options.A: HBeAg (Hepatitis B e antigen)
options.B: Anti-HBs (Hepatitis B surface antibody)
options.C: HBsAg (Hepatitis B surface antigen)
options.D: HBV DNA viral load test

explanation: Checking for anti-HBs shows whether the baby has built up protection after finishing the vaccine doses. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T7#BMP221_U4_T7_h7)

question: A midwife is counseling a couple on the Billings method. Which approach helps ensure success?

options.A: Involving the partner in counseling sessions to encourage shared commitment
options.B: Requiring monthly clinic visits for manual pelvic examinations
options.C: Telling them to memorize complex Latin medical terms for hormones
options.D: Instructing only the woman and forbidding her from discussing it with her partner

explanation: Because the method requires periods of abstinence, joint understanding and agreement between partners greatly increase success rates. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T3#BMP224_U4_T3_h6)

question: A midwife notes that a baby born five minutes ago has a slow heart rate and is struggling to breathe. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait for the attending pediatrician to arrive before touching the infant
options.B: Conduct immediate newborn resuscitation and provide thermal care
options.C: Discharge the mother and baby home immediately to reduce clinic stress
options.D: Prescribe oral antibiotics for suspected neonatal sepsis

explanation: Immediate resuscitation and keeping the newborn warm are core lifesaving responsibilities expected of every trained midwife during intrapartum and neonatal care. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is the Billings method helpful for women with irregular menstrual cycles?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any daily self-observation routine
options.B: It relies on blood tests taken at the end of every month
options.C: It forces the ovaries to release eggs on a fixed schedule
options.D: It tracks real-time body changes instead of relying on past cycle math

explanation: Because it responds to daily physical signs, women do not need predictable cycle lengths to know when they are fertile. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T3#BMP224_U4_T3_h1)

question: Select the correct situation that requires a midwife to use soap and water instead of an alcohol-based hand rub.

options.A: Right before putting on clean non-sterile gloves
options.B: Before entering the neonatal intensive care unit
options.C: When hands are visibly soiled with organic material
options.D: After checking a baby's temperature with an ear thermometer

explanation: Alcohol rubs do not work effectively when dirt, blood, or stool is physically present on the skin, requiring physical washing with soap and water. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T6#BMP220_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why is it best to insert the Copper T 380A during or near the end of menstruation?

options.A: The uterus shrinks to its smallest possible size
options.B: The bleeding helps wash the plastic frame clean
options.C: The cervix is slightly open and pregnancy is unlikely
options.D: The woman feels no pain at all during this time

explanation: Inserting the device during menses makes passage through the cervix easier and provides good reassurance that the client is not pregnant. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T8#BMP224_U3_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core duty of the school midwife or nurse?

options.A: Providing counseling on emotional and physical changes
options.B: Performing major orthopedic surgeries on campus
options.C: Inspecting school water sources and kitchen facilities
options.D: Treating minor injuries and dispensing routine medications

explanation: Major surgeries require specialized hospital theatre setups and are completely outside the scope of school health facilities. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T5#BMP126_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the main job of the costal cartilages in the chest wall?

options.A: Producing red blood cells for the circulatory system
options.B: Preventing the heart from shifting into the right lung
options.C: Anchoring the abdominal muscles to the pelvic girdle
options.D: Providing elasticity to the chest wall during breathing

explanation: Costal cartilages connect the ribs to the breastbone while giving the chest the flexibility to expand and relax as we breathe. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T9#BMP111_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which brain neurotransmitter is most directly linked to the mood changes and cravings seen in PMS?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Serotonin
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Adrenaline

explanation: Falling estrogen levels reduce serotonin activity in the brain, which directly causes irritability, sadness, and carbohydrate cravings. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T5#BMP310_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which type of data works best for a parametric statistical test?

options.A: Nominal data like blood group types A, B, and O
options.B: Categorical data like male or female infant gender
options.C: Continuous numerical data like maternal height
options.D: Ranked data like mild, moderate, or severe pain

explanation: Parametric tests require continuous numerical measurements that follow a normal distribution. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h2)

question: How does hydralazine work on blood vessels to lower blood pressure?

options.A: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme activity
options.B: Direct relaxation of arteriolar smooth muscle
options.C: Blockade of beta-adrenergic receptors in the heart
options.D: Constriction of large capacitance veins

explanation: Hydralazine targets the muscular walls of small blood vessels (arterioles), causing them to relax and widen, which brings the blood pressure down. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T3#BMP213_U3_T3_h1)

question: What does true mental health involve beyond just not having a diagnosed illness?

options.A: A state of emotional and psychological well-being
options.B: Having a completely stress-free lifestyle
options.C: Sleeping for at least ten hours every night
options.D: Never experiencing sadness or worry

explanation: Mental health encompasses emotional and psychological wellness, allowing individuals to cope with normal life stresses rather than simply lacking a disease. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T1#BMP223_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is a key medication given to a newborn born to an HIV-positive mother immediately after birth?

options.A: Administering a full adult dose of antibiotics
options.B: Starting prophylactic antiretroviral syrup
options.C: Providing a concentrated iron supplement
options.D: Giving a therapeutic blood transfusion

explanation: Exposed infants are given antiretroviral prophylaxis shortly after birth to clear any virus that may have entered their system during delivery. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T6#BMP221_U4_T6_h5)

question: What does the practice of open disclosure primarily involve?

options.A: Handing over all personal staff files to the patient's relatives
options.B: Refusing to speak with relatives until an official lawyer arrives
options.C: Transparent and honest communication with families after an adverse event
options.D: Publicly posting hospital error statistics on social media networks

explanation: Open disclosure ensures families receive truthful, empathetic information regarding unexpected complications during maternity care. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the expected pattern of asthma symptom changes across a population of pregnant women?

options.A: Symptoms invariably worsen during the third trimester for every patient
options.B: Most patients experience sudden improvement once progesterone peaks
options.C: One-third improve, one-third worsen, and one-third stay the same
options.D: Nearly all women experience a complete remission of wheezing episodes

explanation: Clinical experience shows that asthma behavior during pregnancy follows a predictable split thirds rule. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T11#BMP221_U4_T11_h2)

question: According to the UNCRC, what is the maximum age for someone to be considered a child?

options.A: Below sixteen years
options.B: Under fifteen years
options.C: Under twenty-one years
options.D: Below eighteen years

explanation: The treaty defines every human being below the age of eighteen as a child, unless local national laws set the age of majority earlier. [learn more](BMP222_U4_T1#BMP222_U4_T1_h1)

question: A young mother requests an intrauterine device, but the midwife refuses, stating she is too young and has no children yet. Which principle has the midwife violated?

options.A: Client autonomy and non-coercive care
options.B: Mandatory hospital documentation guidelines
options.C: Standard infection prevention protocols
options.D: Accurate record keeping standards

explanation: Denying a safe method based on age or parity when medical eligibility criteria are met violates the client's right to autonomous choice. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T1#BMP224_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why do symptoms of uterine prolapse generally improve after the patient rests in bed?

options.A: Fluid retention in the lower body stops completely
options.B: Intra-abdominal pressure increases while sleeping
options.C: The pelvic muscles permanently repair themselves overnight
options.D: Gravity no longer pulls the pelvic organs downward

explanation: Horizontal positioning removes the downward gravitational pull on the unsupported uterus, temporarily relieving pressure. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T12#BMP310_U3_T12_h3)

question: Which vitamin can midwives recommend taking with iron supplements to help the body absorb the iron better?

options.A: Vitamin B12
options.B: Vitamin D
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin K

explanation: Vitamin C creates an acidic environment in the digestive tract, which helps the body absorb oral iron tablets much more effectively. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the main working unit of the kidney that filters blood and makes urine?

options.A: Nephron
options.B: Ureter
options.C: Glomerulus capsule
options.D: Renal pelvis

explanation: The nephron is the microscopic unit in the kidney that handles filtering, reabsorbing, and making urine. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h3)

question: A woman with chronic hypertension at 30 weeks comes to the clinic with a severe headache, blurred vision, and upper belly pain. What condition should the midwife suspect first?

options.A: Normal pregnancy changes
options.B: Superimposed preeclampsia
options.C: Acute uncomplicated malaria
options.D: Severe urinary tract infection

explanation: Epigastric pain, visual disturbances, and severe headaches in a hypertensive pregnant woman are classic warning signs of superimposed preeclampsia. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T3#BMP221_U3_T3_h6)

question: A patient scheduled for morning hemodialysis takes daily blood pressure medication. What is the standard action regarding this medication?

options.A: Crush the pills and mix them directly into the dialysate
options.B: Double the dose to prevent spikes during the treatment
options.C: Administer the medication with extra water immediately
options.D: Hold the medication until after the dialysis session

explanation: Many blood pressure drugs are cleared by dialysis; holding them beforehand prevents sudden, severe drops in blood pressure while fluid is being removed. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T8#BMP216_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why are iodine solutions given to a patient in the days right before a thyroid removal surgery (thyroidectomy)?

options.A: To reduce the size and blood supply of the thyroid gland
options.B: To prevent the development of postoperative infections
options.C: To stimulate the pituitary gland to release extra TSH
options.D: To permanently replace lost parathyroid hormone

explanation: Giving iodine before surgery decreases blood flow to the thyroid, making the procedure safer with less bleeding. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T5#BMP216_U2_T5_h6)

question: What happens in an incomplete abortion?

options.A: The embryo dies inside the uterus but the cervix stays closed
options.B: The pregnancy continues normally despite heavy bleeding
options.C: Some products of conception remain inside the uterus
options.D: All fetal and placental tissues have completely passed out

explanation: An incomplete abortion means part of the pregnancy tissue has come out, but some remains trapped inside the uterine cavity. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the main goal of carrying out a community diagnosis in midwifery?

options.A: To provide free drugs to every household in the district
options.B: To replace the national census figures with local estimates
options.C: To identify local health problems and available community resources
options.D: To punish health workers who fail to meet hospital targets

explanation: A community diagnosis helps find out what health challenges exist locally and what resources are already available to support care. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h1)

question: A woman with severe abruptio placentae develops bleeding from her IV sites and gums because her clotting factors are used up. What is this called?

options.A: Localized vascular spasm
options.B: Uncomplicated primary amenorrhea
options.C: Physiological postpartum diuresis
options.D: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation

explanation: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation is a serious complication where massive clotting uses up available factors, leading to simultaneous bleeding elsewhere. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T9#BMP111_U5_T9_h7)

question: What is a common sign of withdrawal when someone stops taking benzodiazepines suddenly?

options.A: Rigid muscles all over
options.B: Sudden heavy weight gain
options.C: Rebound anxiety and tremors
options.D: Severe permanent hair loss

explanation: Stopping benzodiazepines abruptly makes the nervous system hyperactive, leading to rebound anxiety, shaking, and trouble sleeping. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T4#BMP223_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the main difference between an observational study and an experimental study?

options.A: The researcher does not assign any treatment or intervention
options.B: The study only involves newborn babies and infants
options.C: Data is collected exclusively through laboratory blood tests
options.D: Participants are monitored for exactly twenty-four hours

explanation: Observational studies rely on watching events unfold naturally without the researcher altering care or assigning specific treatments. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T3#BMP225_U2_T3_h1)

question: A student midwife wants to recruit patients from her own antenatal clinic for a study. What ethical issue does she need to watch out for?

options.A: Patients feeling pressured to join because she is their healthcare provider
options.B: Forgetting to check blood pressure
options.C: Losing paper questionnaires on the way to school
options.D: Not paying an administrative fee to the hospital

explanation: Patients might feel forced to join a study if they worry that saying no will affect the medical care they receive from their provider. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T8#BMP225_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the typical average time frame for ovulation to resume after the last dose of DMPA wears off?

options.A: Four to ten months
options.B: Exactly seven days
options.C: Two to three years
options.D: One to two weeks

explanation: Most women begin ovulating again within several months after the drug clears the body, though individual variations occur. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T6#BMP224_U3_T6_h7)

question: How do properly spaced pregnancies directly benefit maternal health?

options.A: They allow the mother's body to recover its nutritional and physical strength
options.B: They prevent the occurrence of all genetic disorders
options.C: They eliminate the need for future antenatal clinic visits
options.D: They guarantee the baby will be born during the dry season

explanation: Adequate birth spacing gives maternal organs and nutrient stores time to recover from the demands of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h6)

question: What makes local transport partnerships essential for rural domiciliary midwifery?

options.A: Rural terrain often lacks standard ambulance services, requiring local solutions
options.B: Local riders do not charge any money for carrying pregnant women
options.C: Motorcycles are faster than helicopters in heavy rainstorms
options.D: Vehicles are always available without prior arrangement

explanation: Because official ambulances are rare in remote areas, partnering with local transport operators is vital for survival. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T2#BMP316_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the main goal of fluid and electrolyte regulation in the body?

options.A: Preventing the digestion of excess dietary proteins
options.B: Maintaining stable water volume and chemical composition
options.C: Slowing down cellular metabolism during resting states
options.D: Increasing the total amount of waste produced daily

explanation: The body keeps water and chemical levels within safe limits so that cells can work normally. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why do operating systems use a desktop layout instead of text commands?

options.A: To make computer navigation more intuitive and accessible for everyday users
options.B: To increase the processing speed of the central processing unit drastically
options.C: To reduce the amount of physical storage space needed on the hard drive
options.D: To eliminate the need for an operating system altogether during startup

explanation: Visual desktops use familiar office concepts so users do not need to memorize complex text commands. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h1)

question: When should palliative care ideally start for someone with a serious, life-limiting illness?

options.A: During the final few weeks of a patient's life
options.B: Only after all curative medical treatments have failed
options.C: Strictly after surgical removal of a primary tumor
options.D: At the time of initial diagnosis alongside curative treatment

explanation: Palliative care runs alongside regular medical treatment to manage symptoms early rather than waiting until the end of life. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T6#BMP320_U2_T6_h1)

question: A woman with a severe fear of medical needles is slowly introduced to looking at pictures of syringes, then sitting near an injection tray, and finally holding an un-capped syringe. What therapeutic approach is being used?

options.A: Electroconvulsive therapy
options.B: Emergency surgical drainage
options.C: Exposure therapy
options.D: Total sensory deprivation

explanation: Gradually facing the feared object in a controlled, step-by-step manner is the core technique of exposure therapy. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T6#BMP223_U3_T6_h6)

question: A youth outreach program has high attendance, but very few teenagers visit the clinic for services. What does this outcome suggest?

options.A: The peer educators are teaching completely accurate and flawless medical facts
options.B: All adolescents in the community are now completely free of health issues
options.C: Barriers still exist between community education and clinic utilization
options.D: The clinic has too many doctors and midwives available for consultations

explanation: A gap between outreach attendance and clinic visits shows that obstacles like fear, stigma, or poor clinic policies are still blocking care. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T7#BMP320_U3_T7_h6)

question: How often should you check the tone of the uterus during the first hour after delivery?

options.A: Every two hours
options.B: Only once at thirty minutes
options.C: Every fifteen minutes
options.D: Every thirty seconds

explanation: Checking every fifteen minutes during the first hour is critical because postpartum hemorrhage most commonly happens in this window. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the main difference between an SGA baby and a premature baby?

options.A: A premature baby always weighs less than 1,000 grams, whereas an SGA baby always weighs over 2,500 grams.
options.B: An SGA baby has completed 40 weeks, while a premature baby has completed less than 30 weeks.
options.C: An SGA baby is always delivered by cesarean section, whereas a premature baby is delivered vaginally.
options.D: An SGA baby has low weight for gestational age, while a premature baby is born before 37 weeks.

explanation: SGA describes slow growth in the womb regardless of when birth happens, while prematurity describes a baby born before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T2#BMP220_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which type of emergency contraceptive pill is most commonly found in Nigerian pharmacies and clinics?

options.A: Progesterone blocking implants
options.B: Combined estrogen-only patches
options.C: Levonorgestrel-only pills
options.D: Ulipristal acetate tablets

explanation: Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg is widely distributed and easily accessible across health facilities and chemist shops in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T10#BMP224_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is the best way to write a subject line when sending an urgent clinical shift swap request?

options.A: Help me please
options.B: Urgent Shift Swap Request: Night Duty on Friday - Midwife Zainab
options.C: Important message from the maternity unit
options.D: My work schedule

explanation: Clear subject lines contain the exact topic, the specific time or date, and your name so the supervisor can act fast. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T3#BMP123_U4_T3_h2)

question: What lifestyle change is a major cause of rising teenage obesity rates in cities?

options.A: The complete elimination of sugary beverages from local markets
options.B: A massive rise in the daily consumption of fresh local vegetables
options.C: Higher levels of rigorous manual farm labor among secondary students
options.D: Increased consumption of processed convenience foods and sedentary habits

explanation: Junk food rich in empty calories paired with less physical movement drives excess weight gain in modern teens. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why is a postpartum tubal ligation often technically easier shortly after vaginal delivery?

options.A: Local anesthesia works much faster on pregnant tissue.
options.B: The fallopian tubes elongate significantly during the third trimester.
options.C: The abdominal wall muscles are permanently weakened by labor.
options.D: The high position of the uterus brings the fallopian tubes close to the navel.

explanation: Right after birth, the fundus remains high, allowing easy access to the tubes through a small incision near the umbilicus. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T12#BMP224_U3_T12_h3)

question: Which term describes blood accumulating inside the pleural space?

options.A: Pneumothorax
options.B: Hemothorax
options.C: Empyema
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: Hemo means blood, and thorax means chest, making hemothorax the medical term for blood in the chest cavity. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T11#BMP125_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why is a minilaparotomy often performed shortly after a woman gives birth?

options.A: Hormonal changes make the fallopian tubes completely insensitive to pain
options.B: The abdominal wall has no nerves at that time, requiring no local anesthesia
options.C: The uterus is still enlarged and brings the fallopian tubes close to the incision
options.D: Postpartum mothers heal completely within twenty-four hours of delivery

explanation: Immediately after delivery, the high position of the fundus makes accessing the fallopian tubes through a small abdominal cut much easier. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h3)

question: A non-pregnant woman taking ciprofloxacin mentions she also takes a daily multi-vitamin with iron and calcium. What advice should the midwife give?

options.A: Take the vitamin only at bedtime while doubling the evening antibiotic dose.
options.B: Crush both tablets together in water to enhance rapid gastrointestinal absorption.
options.C: Stop taking the antibiotic immediately because vitamins deactivate all pills.
options.D: Separate the vitamin and antibiotic doses by at least two hours to prevent chelation.

explanation: Minerals like iron and calcium bind to fluoroquinolones in the gut and prevent proper absorption, so spacing them out is essential. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T7#BMP124_U4_T7_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of school health inspections?

options.A: Prescribing major surgical operations for students
options.B: Controlling the spread of communicable diseases
options.C: Detecting nutritional deficiencies early
options.D: Generating local health baseline statistics

explanation: School inspections focus on screening, prevention, and basic health promotion, not major surgical procedures which belong in hospitals. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T2#BMP126_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why is keeping a newborn warm right after a Caesarean birth so important?

options.A: It replaces the need for routine vitamin K prophylaxis administration
options.B: It directly prevents the development of neonatal jaundice
options.C: It prevents rapid heat loss and dangerous cold stress in the neonate
options.D: It ensures the baby passes meconium within the first hour of life

explanation: Newborns lose heat fast through evaporation; drying and warming them prevents hypothermia and other health issues. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which blood test is known to be specific for diagnosing rheumatoid arthritis early on?

options.A: Liver function panel
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Serum fasting glucose
options.D: Anti-CCP antibodies

explanation: Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies are specific to rheumatoid arthritis and often appear in blood tests before any joint damage shows up on an X-ray. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h3)

question: How do circular folds inside the small intestine help with nutrient absorption?

options.A: They produce bile acids to break down fats
options.B: They directly pump glucose across the cell membrane
options.C: They slow down the movement of digested food to allow more time for uptake

question: Why is it important for midwives to address local dietary taboos during nutrition counseling?
